description: WCAG 2.x contrast ratio. This dataset reproduces a specification rather than a model of perception — ADR-0021 records the decision to enforce WCAG anyway and report APCA alongside. The last entry is the one that justifies the whole design: substituting the engine's exact luminance for WCAG's rounded coefficients flips a real 8-bit colour from AA-failing to AA-passing, so the distinction is a conformance requirement and not pedantry.

entries.source: WCAG 2.x — the maximum possible contrast ratio, and the reason the flare term exists
WCAG 2.x — the minimum possible ratio, for any colour against itself
WCAG 2.x applied to sRGB red against black
entries.derivationNote: Pure red linearises to 1 on the R channel and 0 elsewhere, so L = 0.2126 exactly. (0.2126 + 0.05) / (0 + 0.05) = 0.2626 / 0.05 = 5.252, exactly, with no float64 residue. A useful anchor precisely because it is exact: it fails immediately if the coefficients are wrong.

entries.source: WCAG 2.x — #767676 is the darkest grey commonly cited as passing AA (4.5:1) against white
entries.derivationNote: sRGB [118, 118, 118] / 255. A NEUTRAL, so WCAG's rounded coefficients and the exact sRGB Y row agree to the last bit — which is why greys are safe to check either way and chromatic colours are not.

entries.source: WCAG 2.x applied to sRGB red against white
entries.derivationNote: 3.9984767707539985 — just under 4:1, and frequently quoted as '4:1'. With the exact sRGB Y row it is 3.9978829364 instead. Both are below 4; the pair is here because it is the simplest case where the two coefficient sets visibly differ.

entries.source: WCAG 2.x applied to sRGB blue against white
entries.derivationNote: sRGB blue carries only 7.22% of the luminance, so it contrasts strongly against white despite being a mid-tone to the eye. One of the pairings WCAG models poorly and APCA models better — reported alongside, per ADR-0021.

entries.source: WCAG 2.x §relative luminance versus the exact sRGB-to-XYZ Y row, at sRGB #1B819C on white
entries.derivationNote: rgb(27, 129, 156) against white. With WCAG's published coefficients the ratio is 4.49990508498675, which FAILS AA. With the engine's exact Y row it is 4.500078715444719, which PASSES. A sweep of 8-bit colours against white found 111 such flips across the 3:1, 4.5:1 and 7:1 thresholds. This is why wcag.ts carries its own constants instead of calling srgbToXyz, and why 'the difference is only 5e-4' is not a reason to simplify.
